entries.proposition: The review's own bottom line: whether targeting mitophagy for treatment is more harmful than beneficial is unresolved.
entries.snippet: whether targeting mitophagy for disease treatment is more harmful than beneficial

entries.proposition: The sequence of mitochondrial dysfunction, defective mitophagy and pathogenic protein accumulation is stated as unclear.
entries.snippet: However, the chronological sequence of dysfunctional mitochondria, defective mitophagy and pathongenic proteins is still unclear.
entries.anchor: Mitophagy in chronic diseases of the nervous system

entries.proposition: Mitophagy can occur independently of PINK1, Parkin, or both, in several tissues.
entries.snippet: it has been recently confirmed that mitophagy can occur independently of PINK1, Parkin protein, or both, in a variety of tissues

entries.proposition: NIX/BNIP3 mitophagy is linked to hypoxia and HIF1-alpha stabilisation, the review's only contact with the HIF axis.
entries.snippet: NIX/Bnip3 mediates mitophagy by hypoxia and stabilization of HIF1α

entries.proposition: Acute neurological disease is described as less studied than chronic disease; epilepsy is one of those acute conditions here.
entries.snippet: Compared with chronic diseases of the nervous system, there have been relatively few studies on mitochondrial autophagy in acute diseases of the nervous system.

entries.proposition: Epilepsy paragraph: mutations in the gene for the mTORC1 inhibitor raise susceptibility, without naming the gene.
entries.snippet: In humans, mutations in the gene encoding the mTORC1 autophagy inhibitor are associated with increased susceptibility to epilepsy

entries.proposition: Epilepsy paragraph: rapamycin is called an inducer of mitophagy and is said to prevent epilepsy early and reduce seizures late in mice; the epilepsy evidence is mTOR pathway pharmacology, with no mitophagy measure stated.
entries.snippet: Rapamycin, an inducer of mitophagy and inhibitor of mTOR, can prevent the further development of epilepsy in the early periods

entries.proposition: Table 1 epilepsy row lists rapamycin acting on mTORC1 in a TSC mouse, with the function column giving S6 phosphorylation inhibition.
Typographical error in the text: rapamycin is called 'silomus', and its serious side effects independent of autophagy are noted.
entries.anchor: Mitophagy in chronic diseases of the nervous system

entries.proposition: Figure 2 shows both downregulating mitophagy (3-MA, BNIP3 silencing, WNT3a, glycine) and upregulating it (antagomir, rapamycin, 17-AAG, melatonin, morin, NIX, AMPK, UA/AC, TFEB, PINK1, Atg1, IPC) as leading to neuronal protection, in one schematic with a neuron panel of pathogenic proteins and impaired autophagosome transport; it plots no data.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2: panel A neurological disorders (AD, PD, HD, ALS, stroke, HIE, epilepsy, TBI) to brain, activate mitophagy, deficient mitophagy, cell death; panel B downregulate mitophagy (3-MA, BNIP3-gene silence, WNT3a, glycine) to neuronal protection; panel C upregulate mitophagy (antagomir, rapamycin, 17-AAG, melatonin, morin, NIX, AMPK, UA/AC, TFEB, PINK1, Atg1, IPC) to neuronal protection; panel D a neuron with dysfunctional mitochondria, ROS up and ATP down, pathogenic protein, and sufficient, insufficient or deficient autophagosome transport arrows.

entries.proposition: Figure 1 draws only the PINK1-Parkin-ubiquitin-receptor-LC3 route of mitophagy to autophagosome-lysosome fusion; the text cites it after describing macroautophagy, microautophagy and chaperone-mediated autophagy, which are not drawn.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 1: a sequence of mitochondria with PINK1 (red triangle), phosphorylation (orange), ubiquitination (green), Parkin (blue square), protein receptors (purple), LC3 (wavy) and cardiolipin (cyan), ending in an autophagosome and lysosome fusing; a key in the centre.
